body:
**Credit name.** Doğa Özden ([@dogaozden](https://github.com/dogaozden), https://dogaozden.com/math/live/square-packing/); improved_by Doğa Özden. The result was found by his AI research lab. This issue and the certificate repository were prepared and posted on his behalf by his AI agent, which uses the GitHub account `kenaznia-doga`.

**Claim.** `s(179) ≤ 13.880960371559` (the exact rational side of the witness, rounded up at 12 places). The record holds ` = 13.88379549051089845` (`packing/frontier/n-179.md`, T-174, Nate Chaoweeraprasit's packing (itsnaka), improved by Siddharth Gupta and PingYou Ltd). **The improvement is 2.835e-03** (relative 2.04e-04). **This improves and supersedes our own #954** (n = 179, 13.8813671601098757, pending adoption as T-291 in PR #956): the new side is 4.068e-4 smaller, from the same method on a later batch. #954 stays a verified bound. It is an upper bound only: no KKT, local-optimality, rigidity or global-optimality claim.

**Leaderboard, stated first.** Ours matches the Kaggle leaderboard's side-only entry (13.880960371556, Nevska, 2026-11-07) to about 3e-12 and does not beat it: our exact side is above it by 2.2e-12; the entry is unpublished and unverifiable, ours is a certified packing. Details under "Other public values" below.

**Certificate.** A `Witness/v2` file (corners, rational scalars, 179 squares), `n-179-candidate.yaml`, in https://github.com/kenaznia-doga/s179-upper-bound-13880960371 at commit `6ab3cfe60db4d081092bed3b6bbb44c76b067230` (https://github.com/kenaznia-doga/s179-upper-bound-13880960371/tree/6ab3cfe60db4d081092bed3b6bbb44c76b067230). SHA-256 `77ee3dd21e35ca6abd1410ad3a7ff25b44c5bbc0fe5ebd1031ae112126bf61fc`. `n179-witness.json` is the same file as JSON. The exact coordinates were produced by this repository's own `packing-witness promote --strategy robust-rational` (@ c8448724) from our decimal pose: `center_dilation: '1'`, no dilation, so the pair margins of about 2e-13 are the decimal pose's own (left by the final f64 repair scaling of Evan Daniel's quench, about 1e-13 relative), rounded to 36 digits. The promotion puts the least corner coordinates at 0 and takes the side as the greatest, so only the squares that set the left wall, the bottom wall and the side touch them exactly; other squares near a wall clear it by up to about 1e-12. The decimal pose is in the repository as `n-179-decimal-pose.yaml`, which the witness's `source.path` names; `certificate.replay` names the repository's own file.

**Checking.**
- This repository's `packing-witness verify` (jlevy/squares `main` @ c8448724, run unmodified on the file placed under `packing/witnesses/known-best/`): `VERIFIED`, method exact-algebraic, 15931 pairs tested. Output in `packing-witness-verify.txt`.
- `sqcheck.py` (in the repo), our own exact checker written separately from the registry's code: `VALID`, exact rational. Output in `sqcheck-output.txt`.
- Before promotion, `sqcheck.py` also certified the decimal pose in interval arithmetic at its own side.
- The exact side minus the record's exact side is negative in `Fraction` arithmetic.
- Rerun commands are in the README.

**What the checkers share.** The unit-square, wall and non-overlap definitions only. The promotion to rationals used your tool, so `packing-witness verify` is not independent of how the coordinates were rounded; `sqcheck.py` is.

**Not done.** No local-optimality or rigidity analysis. No formal proof-assistant check. No human review outside our project. We found no open jlevy/squares issue or PR for n = 179 below the record other than our own #954 and its adoption PR #956 (checked c8448724, 2026-11-11 13:30 PST), and nothing better for it in evand/square-packing @ c801ab47.

**Lineage and credit.** The record's holders as the registry lists them: Nate Chaoweeraprasit (itsnaka) (found_by); improved by Siddharth Gupta and PingYou Ltd. Found by an AI-run band-design search, new for this filing (tilted squares from a registry packing of the same family laid along the diagonal as a seed band; simulated annealing in a reduced model in which the tilted squares move freely and the axis-parallel squares sit on the two wall-anchored staircase lattices, present or absent, with the overlap of the squares that must be kept as energy; then one quench with Evan Daniel's ALM+SLP code). This packing was built from the tilted squares of the registry's n = 70 packing (Ryan Xu, found_by; improved by Evan Daniel and PingYou Ltd; side 8.880960371555579595), as in #954: a two-row band of 20 squares at −40.7505° along the diagonal, the band where x + y ≤ 16 plus a second copy shifted by (5, 5) where x + y > 16 (pieces `[70a, 0, 0, 0, 0]` and `[70a, 0, 5, 5, 0]` of our band tool), 35 tilted squares. It came from a later batch of the same scan as a mutation of such a seed (band parameter 4.4245 where #954's seed has 4.2495), annealed at side 13.88105 (3e6 moves, energy 0.0035), then quenched to 13.880960371558. Two further jobs of the batch reach the same side (to 1.5e-13) from the same band and from a different one (`179ha`/`207a`, shifted by (−1, −1)). The packing keeps one straight band of tilted squares from corner to corner like #954's, but its side is 4.07e-4 below it. Its side is 2.64e-12 above side(70) + 5 = 13.880960371555579595, and we have not shown that the packing is that construction. Squares matched by assignment up to the symmetries of the square: 143 of 179 centres move by more than 1e-3, 48 by more than 0.05 (largest 0.889); 43 squares are re-tilted by more than 1° (largest 44.36°); the packing has 36 squares tilted by more than 0.5° against the record's 35. See `records/n-179-candidate-diff.png`. Credit the improvement to Doğa Özden, the band's source packing to n = 70 (Ryan Xu; improved by Evan Daniel and PingYou Ltd) and the current record to its holders as the registry lists them, and the local optimizer to Evan Daniel (`search/packer`, MIT, @ bb4cc78e).

**Licence.** The repository carries `LICENSE.md`: CC BY 4.0 for the witness, data and text; MIT for code. It also carries Evan Daniel's MIT notice, `LICENSE-evand-square-packing.txt`.

**Other public values, for context.** The best public Kaggle per-puzzle packing we found for 179 has side 13.883795490524 (kirilltym; dataset refreshed 2026-11-11 03:32Z), above ours. The Kaggle per-puzzle leaderboard (staff notebook inversion/squares-in-squares-per-puzzle-leaderboard; cache of 2026-11-09 20:52Z) lists a side-only entry for n = 179: **13.880960371556**, team Nevska, 2026-11-07. It is unpublished and states no packing, so we cannot verify it and make no claim about it. **Ours matches it to about 3e-12 and does not beat it:** our exact side 13.880960371558224 (claim, rounded up: 13.880960371559) is above it by 2.2e-12 (3e-12 for the claim). Its fractional part is that of the registry's n = 70 and n = 207 sides (0.880960371556), as ours now is to 12 places. This improves our own #954 (13.881367160110) by 4.07e-4 and the registry record by 2.84e-3; it is the best published packing with a certificate we know of, not a side below the leaderboard's.

**AI assistance.** Yes, throughout. The search and its code were written and run by AI agents; the checks above were run by code that did not produce the packing. Doğa directed the work and asked that our results be registered.
title: s(179) ≤ 13.880960371559: improved packing (registration request)
